description: Lightweight string utility atoms that keep string contents opaque and expose only Z3-friendly i64 facts for std/string expansion. This task deliberately avoids unimplemented string-theory operators: safe_truncate returns a validated length bound supplied by callers, character predicates classify one ASCII code point, and length-composition helpers operate only on caller-supplied bounds. The generated file MUST begin with a header comment block (// ======) identifying the module as 'std/string_utils — verified string utilities'. Comments must be in Japanese to match the surrounding std style. Each atom follows the convention used in std/core.mm: `atom name(params) requires: ...; ensures: ...; body: { ... };`. Do NOT invent new operators, types, or syntax — use only conditionals, comparisons, conjunction, disjunction, and integer constants already present in std/core.mm.
implementation_notes: Do not access Str internals or call undefined len/substring methods.
safe_truncate may return max_len directly because callers provide max_len as the bound to be preserved.
is_ascii should check 0 <= code && code <= 127 and return an i64 boolean.
Length helpers must use caller-provided lengths and caps only; never synthesize real string concatenation.

atoms.name: safe_truncate
atoms.description: Return a trusted truncated length bound supplied by the caller. Output is non-negative and never exceeds max_len, so callers can use it as a slice bound without further checks.

atoms.name: is_ascii
atoms.description: Return 1 if `code` is in the ASCII byte range [0, 127], otherwise 0. The boolean is encoded as i64 so the contract is provable with Z3 integer theory.

atoms.name: is_hex_ascii_code
atoms.description: Return 1 when an ASCII code is a hexadecimal digit [0-9a-fA-F], otherwise 0. The boolean is encoded as i64 and uses only integer comparisons.

atoms.name: bounded_concat_len
atoms.description: Combine two caller-provided non-negative string lengths while proving the result remains within the supplied cap.
atoms.requires: left_len >= 0 && right_len >= 0 && max_len >= 0 && left_len + right_len <= max_len
